profile.reading:
This OSM record, "Switch Edge 1," is tagged near Switch's Las Vegas Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, with an address of 5325 West Capovilla Avenue previously corroborated by a reverse geocode and a third-party aggregator listing for a facility by that name. However, further research this session found that Switch's own current website describes "Switch Edge" as a product line, not a fixed numbered building: Switch markets it as "the world's only Class 4, system-plus-system, air-transportable edge data center platform," built from container-like "Switch MOD 15" modular pods intended for rapid, portable deployment rather than a permanent campus structure. No page or press release on switch.com names a specific, permanently sited "Switch Edge 1" facility, and this session could not confirm whether the aggregator-sourced name and address represent an actual deployed unit at that location, a demonstration unit, or a naming convention applied by a third party rather than by Switch itself. Given the shared 5325 West Capovilla Avenue address with the separately tracked Las Vegas 12 building in this same dataset, this record may represent either a genuinely distinct smaller edge deployment co-located with Las Vegas 12, or a duplicate/mislabeled record referring to the same physical site; this profile does not resolve that ambiguity and flags it explicitly rather than asserting either possibility as fact. No independent square footage, megawatt, or Tier certification figure could be confirmed for this record specifically.

Switch's broader Las Vegas Core Campus, of which the confirmed Las Vegas 12 building sits nearby sharing the same street, has grown from Rob Roy's original 2002 acquisition of a former Enron-affiliated facility into eleven or more operating buildings spanning well over 2 million square feet, with current marketing describing up to 495 megawatts of power available upon full campus completion. Switch has more recently begun developing dedicated smaller "AI Factory" buildings on nearby Jones Boulevard and Roy Horn Way, announced July 2025, roughly 199,000 and 228,000 square feet respectively, illustrating a shift in Switch's Las Vegas product mix toward denser, AI-specific infrastructure alongside legacy general-purpose colocation buildings, a category this smaller "Edge" designation may or may not be part of.

reading.body:
This record identifies a facility called Switch Edge 1 at an address shared with the separately tracked Las Vegas 12 building, but Switch's own website describes Edge as a product line of modular, portable data center pods rather than a named permanent facility. No page on switch.com confirms a specific building called Edge 1, and research this session could not determine whether this address represents a distinct co-located deployment, a demonstration unit, or a data-entry duplicate. The operator has published no megawatt capacity figure for this facility.

Switch's broader Las Vegas Core Campus, which operates multiple buildings on this campus, has marketed up to 495 megawatts of total power availability at full completion. The campus has been in operation since 2002 and now spans over 2 million square feet across eleven or more buildings. Switch recently announced dedicated AI-specific facilities nearby, suggesting a product shift toward denser infrastructure for machine learning workloads, though it is not published whether this Edge designation falls within that category.

Nevada has only 2 data center facilities with published power capacity figures in this site's dataset, and this facility's capacity is not one of them. Without a confirmed megawatt figure or independent verification that Switch Edge 1 exists as a distinct physical site rather than a product category or a mislabeled record, this facility cannot be ranked among Nevada's published capacity or assessed for relevance to AI infrastructure scaling in the state.
